name: WCAG 2.1 for Web Apps & Power Platform
description: Makes everything the agent builds or reviews conform to WCAG 2.1 AA — HTML pages, SPAs, theming, PCF controls, model-driven and canvas apps, and Power Pages.
author: Mark Christie
coverImageAlt: Four accessibility mechanisms converge on one high-contrast open frame with a smooth navigation path and tactile controls.
coverImagePrompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: AI.Tedt.org skill gallery cover
Primary request: Create a premium editorial illustration that communicates accessibility being engineered into every web and business-app component from the beginning.
Scene/backdrop: A warm paper-toned component workshop with modular panels, controls, navigation paths, and content blocks assembled as physical objects rather than a literal interface.
Subject: A central open frame is supported by four coordinated accessibility mechanisms: a high-contrast focus ring, a smooth ramp-like navigation path, tactile controls with generous spacing, and a sculptural sound wave paired with a clear visual signal; all paths converge through the same usable opening.
Style/medium: Premium editorial illustration with tactile dimensional detail, layered cut paper, matte ceramic controls, translucent acrylic focus layers, precise inclusive-design craftsmanship, sophisticated rather than playful.
Composition/framing: Exact 16:10 landscape; central accessible frame dominates; four mechanisms balance around it in a clear system; strong contrast and generous spacing; crop-safe focal subject; no essential detail in the outer 8%.
Lighting/mood: Calm, capable, quietly technical; bright even studio light, assured clarity, humane and rigorous.
Color palette: Warm paper #F8F6F0, slate #101820, navy #00446F, cyan #00A9E0, sparing orange #E86027, with contrast relationships that remain visually distinct.
Constraints: No text, letters, numbers, logos, trademarks, or watermark; no paw imagery or paw logo; no cats or cat silhouettes; no product UI or Microsoft Fluent branding. Do not use a wheelchair icon, compliance badge, checklist text, browser chrome, or a literal software screenshot.
